title: personal-rhythm-performance-manifesto
content:
Personal rhythm — lightweight manifesto and prep for 1:1s

Aim: keep a compact, signal-first record of weekly progress, short-term experiments, and concrete manager asks. Avoid long essays; capture proof + pragmatic next steps.

Weekly checkpoints (5–10 mins):
- Wins: 1–2 concrete outcomes with metric or impact (who benefited).
- Blockers: 1 thing needing manager unblock or priority trade.
- Learning: quick note (what I tried, what I observed).
- Small ask: 1 micro-request (time, intro, approval).

Thirty-minute 1:1 template (my prep):
- Two-minute headline: current sprint focus + any immediate risk.
- Evidence bullets (30–90s each):
  * Onboarding revamp pilot: reduced new-hire first-week setup steps from 11 to 6 (measured by new-hire survey N=8). Draft checklist: link to PR.
  * People ops SLO dashboard: built initial metrics for time-to-offer and offer acceptance cadence (alpha). Observed 12% drop in time-to-offer for Eng interns during pilot.
- Ask bank (ranked):
  1) Approve headcount justification for contract recruiter (2 months) — request: $18k.
  2) Time for shadowing: 4 hours with Talent Partner lead next sprint.
  3) Sign-off on comms draft for onboarding changes (small rewrite).
- Career checkpoint (2–3 signals):
  * Leadership: ran cross-functional onboarding working group (5 meetings) and delivered checklist + automation spec.
  * Execution: shipped onboarding docs + tracked adoption across two cohorts.
  * Coaching ask: need feedback on delegation — where I can push decisions down quicker.

Quarterly micro-plan (90-day lens):
- North star: shorten time-to-ramp for new hires from 45 days -> 30 days for standard ICs.
- Key initiatives:
  1) Onboarding breathwork (doc + infra): automate account provisioning steps via internal ticket templates.
  2) Manager enablement: 3 micro-workshops with engineering managers focused on 15-minute onboarding checklists.
  3) HL metrics: finalize dashboard, instrument baseline, and set targets.
- Success metrics (quantitative + qualitative):
  * Time-to-first-PR, time-to-ship (first minor change), new hire NPS >= 8.0 (target).
  * Manager confidence score (survey) + concrete reduction in support tickets for day‑1 access.

Concrete stories (for calibration / promotion narrative):
- Story A (cross-team coordination): Led the onboarding automation spec — coordinated infra, security, and SRE to remove 3 manual SLA steps. Outcome: first-week access incidents decreased 60% for pilot cohort.
- Story B (impact under ambiguity): When intern hiring surged, I scoped a lightweight intake + prioritization doc that reduced recruiter churn and kept offer velocity steady.

Evidence index (quick links + numbers):
- Onboarding checklist PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/people-ops/pull/45
- Time-to-offer dashboard (alpha): Confluence draft id CONFLUENCE-PEOPLE-012 (see linked_artifacts)
- New-hire survey raw notes (summary): +8 NPS for cohort 1 vs baseline

Risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: Airing changes without manager alignment -> confusion across teams. Mitigation: run 15-minute manager sync, collect feedback, iterate doc before wide rollout.
- Risk: Over-promising automation in Q3 -> deprioritizes other ops work. Mitigation: ship 1 durable automation + several low-effort fixes; re-evaluate scope mid-quarter.

Quick coaching asks for next 1:1: 
1) How did I do in prioritizing the hiring backlog? Specific example: choosing to triage the recruitment apps flow vs the access flow.
2) One thing I can stop doing this month (time sink).
3) Intro to Cara (Eng manager) to pilot manager enablement session.

To-dos (next 14 days):
- Finalize recruiter contract justification doc and attach budget numbers (due: 2025-09-18).
- Run pilot manager workshop (target date 2025-09-25).
- Instrument one more metric on the dashboard (time-to-first-PR).
- Synthesize feedback from cohort 1 survey and produce 1-page comms for company-wide rollout.

Notes to self (short):
- Keep evidence short: 3 bullets per story max.
- Ask concretely: time, approval, intro (not broad).
- Use quantitative + qualitative combo.

Open questions (for scribble later):
- Is 30 days ramp realistic for mid-SEs given current infra constraints? (need baseline by role).
- Who is the authoritative owner for laptop provisioning flow? I have a partial map but not full owner list.

End-of-doc micro-reflection:
If I can free up one day a week from repetitive ops work by Q4, I can invest that time into manager coaching and process design work that scales. This feels like the lever that unlocks the next level of impact for the team.

(Version history: created as a working scratchpad — meant to be short-lived and iterated with manager after each 1:1.)
